title: Job stores never evict: four module-global Maps grow for the life of the server
body:
## Summary
The tripo, triposr, hunyuan and trellis job Maps have no eviction.

## Description
Each store sets one entry per job and never deletes (src/lib/visual-gen/tripo-job-store.ts:85, src/lib/visual-gen/triposr-job-store.ts:45, src/lib/visual-gen/hunyuan-job-store.ts:46, src/lib/visual-gen/trellis-job-store.ts:82). Each entry keeps its full spec and critique. A bounded retention of finished jobs would cap it.

## Flow
- Run N generations in one server life
- Map size equals N because no delete site exists

## Expected impact
Long-lived dev servers stop accumulating job records. An evicted id would read as unknown to a status poll, so the bound must outlast any client poll window.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - bounded job retention
Before: 4 of 4 stores have 0 delete sites; memory per job not sampled
After: not measured until a cap exists
Method: simulation - read the stores; heap effect needs an instrument
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Map.size and heap after 1000 stubbed jobs before and after a cap, plus a status poll against an evicted id

title: Three local job stores repeat one settle lifecycle by hand
body:
## Summary
The triposr, hunyuan and trellis stores each copy the run, critique, summarize and settle block.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/triposr-job-store.ts:61, src/lib/visual-gen/hunyuan-job-store.ts:62 and src/lib/visual-gen/trellis-job-store.ts:101 hold the same block. The critic-throw fix had to be applied three times tonight (38e479264). A shared settle helper makes the next gate change single-site.

## Flow
- Extract a settleLocalJob helper
- Point the three stores at it and keep their per-provider spec types

## Expected impact
A gate rule change lands once instead of three times. Break risk is covered by a shared store test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one lifecycle site
Before: 3 copies of about 20 lines; 1 fix applied 3 times tonight
After: 1 site (estimate, not built)
Method: simulation - counted the copies, did not build the extraction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Line count plus one parametrised test over all three stores after extraction

title: Tripo status unknown is terminal and drops recoverability
body:
## Summary
TERMINAL_FAIL includes unknown, so a task Tripo cannot describe ends with recoverable false.

## Description
parseTaskStatus classes unknown with failed, cancelled, banned and expired (src/lib/visual-gen/tripo-runner.ts, TERMINAL_FAIL) and pollTripoTask marks that non-recoverable. The word suggests the provider has no current verdict, the condition the transient state exists for, but no live response has been sampled and tests pin it as failed.

## Flow
- Sample what Tripo returns for a task reporting unknown
- If such tasks later complete, move unknown to transient and update the two pinning tests

## Expected impact
A paid task would stay recoverable instead of being abandoned. If unknown is truly terminal nothing changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - keep paid handles
Before: unknown is terminal; pinned at src/__tests__/lib/visual-gen/tripo-runner.test.ts:113 and :509
After: depends on provider behaviour
Method: simulation - needs a live provider observation this round must not make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: Operator-only: a live poll log of a Tripo task that reported unknown

title: SkinTokens crash list omits other Windows fatal exit codes
body:
## Summary
Only access violation counts as a retryable crash.

## Description
SKINTOKENS_CRASH_EXIT_CODES (src/lib/visual-gen/skintokens-runner.ts:133) lists SIGSEGV and 0xC0000005 in two spellings. A stack overrun (0xC0000409), heap corruption (0xC0000374) or illegal instruction (0xC000001D) would read as a real error and not retry, on a backend measured as nondeterministically unstable. Whether those codes occur here has not been observed.

## Flow
- Log exit codes over a batch of Vulkan runs
- Add any fatal NTSTATUS actually seen

## Expected impact
Fewer rigs lost to a non-retried crash, if those codes occur.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - retry every crash exit
Before: 3 listed codes; other fatal codes unobserved
After: unknown until sampled
Method: simulation - requires real Vulkan runs this round must not spawn
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Operator-only: exit-code histogram from a real Vulkan batch

title: TRELLIS.2 WSL argv with spaces is unverified
body:
## Summary
wsl.exe re-parses its command line, so a path containing spaces may split.

## Description
runTrellis spawns wsl.exe -d distro -- py args (src/lib/visual-gen/trellis-runner.ts:173) with paths translated by toWslPath. The UE project sits under a path with a space (Unreal Projects); the generated output path has none today, so this is latent.

## Flow
- Spawn wsl.exe to print an argv containing a space
- If it splits, quote it or pass through a script

## Expected impact
Prevents a confusing argparse failure for an image outside the repo.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - argv fidelity across WSL
Before: not measured; no WSL spawn permitted in this round
After: echo probe result
Method: simulation - walked the argv only
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: No-GPU probe: wsl.exe -d <distro> -- printf with one spaced argument

title: Qwen output is named .png unsniffed while Leonardo sniffs its bytes
body:
## Summary
generateTwoDImage trusts the DashScope format for Qwen and magic-numbers Leonardo.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/image-providers.ts:332 fixes the name to png on the comment that DashScope returns PNG, while :369 uses sniffImageExt so a Leonardo JPEG is never labelled png. The Qwen name is chosen before the bytes exist, so the runner must report the real format.

## Flow
- Have runQwenImage report the sniffed extension
- Name the file after the download

## Expected impact
A mislabelled image becomes impossible on the Qwen path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one format rule for both providers
Before: 1 of 2 providers sniffs
After: 2 of 2 (not built)
Method: simulation - the format claim comes from a dated live check, not re-probed
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Stubbed runner test feeding JPEG bytes through generateTwoDImage
